from doorstop.core import Document, Item, Tree, build, importer, exporter, publisher

from doorstop.core.tree import Tree as TreeCls
from doorstop.core.vcs import mockvcs  # use the mock VCS for deterministic behaviour


# Helper to create a minimal requirement document in a temporary directory
def create_doc(tmp_path: Path, prefix: str = "REQ") -> DocCls:
    """Create a new Doorstop document with a single requirement."""
    doc_path = tmp_path / f"{prefix}.md"
    # The Document.new method expects a path and optional prefix
    doc = DocCls.new(tmp_path, prefix=prefix)
    # Add a single item
    item = doc.add_item("Initial requirement")
    # Save the document (and the item file)
    doc.save()
    return doc


@pytest.fixture
def temp_dir(tmp_path):
    """Return a temporary directory for tests."""
    return tmp_path


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Test cases derived from the abstract test cases
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

def test_U02_4__Gherkin_BDD___TC_001(temp_dir):
    """
    Doorstop stores requirements in a permanent and secure manner
    """
    # Create a document and add a requirement
    doc = create_doc(temp_dir)
    # The requirement file should exist in the document directory
    req_files = list(doc.path.glob("*.md"))
    assert req_files, "No requirement files found in the document directory"
    # Ensure the file is not in a temporary or volatile location
    # (here we simply check that the path is absolute and under the temp dir)
    for f in req_files:
        assert f.is_absolute()
        assert f.parent == doc.path


def test_U02_4__Gherkin_BDD___TC_002(temp_dir):
    """
    Doorstop handles change management of the requirements
    """
    doc = create_doc(temp_dir)
    # Get the first item
    item = doc.items[0]
    original_text = item.text
    # Modify the requirement text
    item.text = "Updated requirement text"
    # Save changes
    doc.save()
    # Reload the item from disk to verify persistence
    reloaded_item = ItemCls.load(item.path)
    assert reloaded_item.text == "Updated requirement text"
    assert reloaded_item.text != original_text
